chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mihran, who said:

A man wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the Second, complaining to him of his bereavement with his son and the intensity of the grief that had entered him. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Do you not know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chooses from the wealth of the Believer and from his children, his soul, in order to recompense him for that?'

key_terms.أَنْفَسَهُ: his soul (referring to the deceased person)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah take the soul of a believer's child or wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of divine selection (ikhtiyar), where Allah chooses the best souls of believers to be taken from this world, thereby granting them a superior reward for their loss. It reframes bereavement not merely as a trial but as an honor, emphasizing that the deceased's spiritual status is elevated through this divine choice, a view supported by the Imams' teachings on the virtue of the righteous dead.
